41-in the cluster.
42-NNG’s determination of the boundaries for a Class 2 or 3 area was not consistent with the
43-class location criteria as required by § 192.5(c)(2). Specifically, NNG utilized clustering
44-to reduce the size of a Class 2 or 3 area, which is allowed by the regulations. However,
45-NNG’s procedure 80.101 for class location determination, which cross-referenced NNG’s
46-Engineering Standard (ES) 0060, allowed NNG to utilize three (3) buildings as the
47-minimum size for the cluster. This methodology allowed NNG to reduce the class
48-location of areas with occupied buildings that were originally classed to a higher class
49-location by the original sliding mile analysis. § 192.5(c)(2) indicates that the length of
50-Class locations 2, 3, and 4 can be adjusted, but operators cannot downgrade the actual
51-class location. As a result, the true length of the Class 2 or 3 location may not be defined
52-correctly because those three or less buildings would have extended the length of the
53-Class 2 or 3 location.
54-During PHMSA’s inspection, inspectors reviewed NNG’s class locations in random areas
55-of the NNG pipeline system and identified two locations (three examples) where
56-clustering was used to reduce the length of a Class 3 area, because there were less than

70-In the above examples, NNG’s clustering methodology allowed the class locations in all
71-examples to be derated from Class 3 to Class 1. In looking at the Class 1 area directly
72-adjacent to the Class 3 areas, there were occupied structures (less than three) where the
73-class reduction occurred. All the structures were within the original sliding mile for a
74-Class 3. NNG’s ES 0060, referenced from procedure 80.101, allowed the location of
75-these buildings to be downgraded from a Class 3 to a Class 1 area, thereby reducing the
76-true length of the Class 3 area.
77-By using a methodology that allowed three buildings to be clustered, NNG downgraded
78-multiple Class 3 locations, in violation of § 192.5(c)(2).

149-Pursuant to 49 United States Code § 60118, the Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety
150-Administration (PHMSA) proposes to issue to NNG a Compliance Order incorporating the
151-following remedial requirements to ensure the compliance of NNG with the pipeline safety
152-regulations:
153-A.
154-
155-In regard to Item 1 of the Notice pertaining to the incorrect application of class
156-location clustering, NNG must do the following:
157-• Revise ES 0060, which is referenced from Procedure 80.101, to ensure
158-that any class location with occupied structures established from the
159-original sliding mile analysis is not derated to a lower class location for
160-any reason.
161-• Submit the revision within 90 days of receipt of the Final Order.
162-• Train NNG personnel on the new procedure and submit the training
163-records within 150 days of receipt of the Final Order.
164-• Implement and complete the new procedure system wide to re-evaluate the
165-lengths of the existing Class 2 and 3 locations upon completion of the
166-revised procedures.
167-• Provide PHMSA a quarterly update on the status of the re-evaluation.
168-• The revised evaluation of the system must be completed within 360 days
169-of the receipt of the Final Order. Any requests for an extension must be
170-made a minimum of 30 days in advance.
171-
172-B.
173-
174-It is requested that NNG maintain documentation of the safety improvement costs
175-associated with fulfilling this Compliance Order and submit the total to Gregory
176-A Ochs, Director, Central Region, Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety
177-Administration. It is requested that these costs be reported in two categories: (1)
178-total cost associated with preparation/revision of plans, procedures, studies and
179-analyses, and (2) total cost associated with replacements, additions and other
180-changes to pipeline infrastructure.
